A to-one association is eager by default, so reading one row reads its whole parent chain. Declare fetch = FetchType.LAZY, or FetchType.EAGER when that is genuinely wanted.
Cascading a delete across a to-many association removes rows the parent does not own. Use orphanRemoval = true, or delete the children explicitly.

A repository method returning an unbounded collection reads as many rows as the table holds. Take a Pageable.
A query built by concatenation puts its operand into the statement rather than into a parameter. Bind the value with a named parameter instead.
An AUTO or absent generation strategy resolves differently per dialect, and TABLE serialises every insert. Declare IDENTITY or SEQUENCE.

message.value: Several pagination parameters share one request namespace. Give each a non-empty @Qualifier.

property.name: query
property.value: //PARAMETER_DEF[./MODIFIERS/ANNOTATION/IDENT[@text='RequestParam' or @text='PathVariable' or @text='RequestHeader' or @text='CookieValue'] and ./MODIFIERS/ANNOTATION/IDENT[@text='AssertFalse' or @text='AssertTrue' or @text='DecimalMax' or @text='DecimalMin' or @text='Digits' or @text='Email' or @text='Future' or @text='FutureOrPresent' or @text='Max' or @text='Min' or @text='Negative' or @text='NegativeOrZero' or @text='NotBlank' or @text='NotEmpty' or @text='NotNull' or @text='Null' or @text='Past' or @text='PastOrPresent' or @text='Pattern' or @text='Positive' or @text='PositiveOrZero' or @text='Size'] and not(ancestor::CLASS_DEF/MODIFIERS/ANNOTATION/IDENT[@text='Validated'])]

message.value: A constraint on a bound parameter is evaluated only where the declaring class carries @Validated, so this one rejects nothing. Add @Validated to the class.
A handler @RequestMapping naming no method answers every HTTP verb. Use @GetMapping, @PostMapping or the sibling that states the verb.
A single-verb handler should use @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @DeleteMapping or @PatchMapping instead of @RequestMapping.
A @CrossOrigin with no origin, or with a wildcard, admits every origin. Name the origins the endpoint serves.
An HTTP client built at a call site carries its own connection pool and no shared timeouts. Declare it once as a @Bean and take it as a constructor parameter.
A servlet type in a handler signature ties the controller to the container and hides the value it actually wanted. Declare that value as a parameter instead.

property.name: message
property.value: Disabling CSRF for the whole chain is right only when no cookie authenticates a request. Scope the exemption with ignoringRequestMatchers instead.

property.name: message
property.value: Permitting every request makes the rest of the filter chain decorative. Name the public paths and leave anyRequest authenticated.

property.name: message
property.value: Ignoring a path removes it from the filter chain entirely, headers and audit included. Use permitAll on that path instead.

property.name: message
property.value: This encoder either stores a recoverable password or uses a default work factor. Use BCrypt, PBKDF2 or Argon2 with an explicit strength.

property.name: message
property.value: Disabling this response header removes a protection the browser applies for free. Keep it, and use sameOrigin where a frame is genuinely wanted.

message.value: A signing or encryption key written as a literal ships with the artifact that uses it. Read it from configuration.

property.name: message
property.value: Permitting the actuator prefix publishes the environment, the beans and the mappings. Name the health probes individually and leave the rest authenticated.

property.name: message
property.value: An in-memory user ships a working credential with the artifact. Load users from the system that owns them.

message.value: A private scheduled method breaks as soon as anything causes the bean to be proxied, because the invocation lands on the proxy rather than on the instance holding the state. Make the method public.
A scheduled method takes no arguments, because the scheduler has nothing to pass it. Read what the method needs from a collaborator instead.

property.name: query
property.value: //METHOD_DEF[./MODIFIERS/ANNOTATION/IDENT[@text='Scheduled'] and not(./TYPE/LITERAL_VOID) and not(./TYPE/IDENT[@text='Publisher' or @text='Mono' or @text='Flux' or @text='Single' or @text='Maybe' or @text='Completable' or @text='Observable' or @text='Flowable'])]

message.value: Nothing receives what a scheduled method returns. Return void and record the outcome where something reads it, or return a Publisher, which the scheduler subscribes to on the schedule.
A schedule written as a literal cannot differ between environments. Read it from a property placeholder.
A scheduled task names no scheduler, so a later bean can retarget it. Declare scheduler with a non-empty property placeholder.
A cron expression with no zone runs in the scheduler process zone. Declare zone with a property placeholder.

property.value: //ANNOTATION[./IDENT[@text='Scheduled'] and ./ANNOTATION_MEMBER_VALUE_PAIR/IDENT[@text='fixedRate' or @text='fixedRateString' or @text='fixedDelay' or @text='fixedDelayString' or @text='initialDelay' or @text='initialDelayString'] and not(./ANNOTATION_MEMBER_VALUE_PAIR/IDENT[@text='timeUnit'])]

message.value: A fixed schedule with no timeUnit interprets a bare configured value as milliseconds. Declare the intended TimeUnit.
A private listener breaks as soon as anything causes the bean to be proxied, because the invocation lands on the proxy rather than on the instance holding the state. Make the method public.

property.name: query
property.value: //METHOD_DEF[./MODIFIERS/ANNOTATION[./IDENT[@text='EventListener']] and (count(./PARAMETERS/PARAMETER_DEF) > 1 or count(./PARAMETERS/PARAMETER_DEF) = 0 and not(./MODIFIERS/ANNOTATION[./IDENT[@text='EventListener']]/EXPR) and not(./MODIFIERS/ANNOTATION[./IDENT[@text='EventListener']]/ANNOTATION_MEMBER_VALUE_PAIR[./IDENT[@text='value' or @text='classes']]))]

message.value: An @EventListener takes the event alone, and Spring refuses the context otherwise. Take one parameter, or name the event classes in the annotation and take none.
A listener writing inside the publisher transaction ties the two together in both directions. Use @TransactionalEventListener and say which phase it runs in.
A transactional listener inherits when it runs and whether non-transactional events are discarded. Declare phase and fallbackExecution explicitly.
An @InitBinder method returns nothing, and Spring refuses the context otherwise. Configure the WebDataBinder it is given and return void.

property.name: message
property.value: A thread the container did not create misses graceful shutdown, metrics and the security context. Take a TaskExecutor bean and submit to it.

message.value: This Spring Boot test annotation already applies SpringExtension. Remove SpringExtension from @ExtendWith and retain any other extensions.
An @Sql with an inferred resource or phase changes under a test rename. Name scripts or statements and executionPhase explicitly.
A rolled-back test never commits, so nothing that happens at commit is exercised. Let the test commit and clean up after itself.

Inline test properties give this class its own application context rather than the shared one. Declare them once on a composed annotation that each test carries, which names the same context without a shared base class.
A transaction hook returns void and takes no arguments, and Spring raises otherwise. Correct the signature.

property.name: message
property.value: Discarding the application context makes every later test class pay a fresh startup. Leave the context as the test found it.

property.name: message
property.value: This starts no server, so the filter chain, the serialisation and the error handling are simulated rather than exercised. Use @SpringBootTest with a random port and a real client.

property.name: message
property.value: This binds the Jackson 2 mapper, which Boot does not auto-configure, so every spring.jackson setting applies to a mapper this code never uses. Import the tools.jackson package instead.

message.value: The scan root is already fixed by airness.package.root, so naming a base package here either restates it or overrides it. Remove the attribute.

property.name: message
property.value: A disabled test reports as absent rather than as failing. Fix it, delete it, or gate it on a platform condition such as @DisabledOnOs.

property.name: message
property.value: A failed assumption aborts a test and reports it as passed. Gate the test on a platform condition, or set up what it needs.

property.name: message
property.value: A commented-out test stopped running and stopped being visible at the same time. Restore it or delete it.

property.name: message
property.value: A sleep makes the verdict depend on the speed of the machine. Wait on the condition itself instead.

property.name: message
property.value: Unseeded randomness makes a suite that passes today fail on some later run. Seed it with a fixed value, as in new Random(42).
